Enron.desc: A United States energy company based in Houston which traded energy and at its zenith drew 80% of its revenue from trading; it was once the largest energy trader in the world. It filed for bankruptcy on 4 December 2001, listing assets of $49.8 billion and debts of $31.2 billion.

Kuala Lumpur Kepong Berhad's mandatory cash offer completed on 23 December 2013, leaving it with 63.2% of the shares, and it held about 62.9% in May 2020, when the company proposed selling its remaining 50% interest in the Liberian joint venture to KLK Agro Plantations for 1 pound; a completion of disposal notice is dated 11 June 2020.

Essar Power (Essar Power MP).desc: An Indian electricity generating business; Essar Power Ltd is described as one of India's largest private-sector power producers, owning plants in India and Canada with a total planned generation capacity of 5,090 MW, of which 3,830 MW was operational when this was reported in August 2017. Essar Power MP Ltd operates the 2x600 MW Mahan power plant in Singrauli district, Madhya Pradesh.

Esso Highlands Limited (ExxonMobil PNG).desc: An oil and gas company described by ExxonMobil as an ExxonMobil subsidiary; in 2009 it held a 33.2% participating interest in the PNG LNG project in Papua New Guinea and acted as its operator.

Eurasian Resources Group (ERG).desc: A mining and natural-resources group headquartered in Luxembourg, with mining, processing, energy, logistics and marketing operations; it is one of the world's largest producers of cobalt and ferrochrome and a supplier of copper, iron ore and alumina. The Government of Kazakhstan holds 40%, and the group said in 2024 that over 80,000 people work for it worldwide.

Everland.desc: A marketing company registered as Everland LLC and headquartered in New York City, which markets REDD+ forest conservation projects and the verified emission reductions (carbon credits) they generate, with projects in Africa, Asia and Latin America. Ecuacorriente operates the $1 billion Mirador open-pit copper mine in Zamora-Chinchipe, expected to produce about 100,000 tonnes of copper a year at full capacity (2019); Explorcobres S.A. is the consortium's subsidiary for the San Carlos-Panantza project in Morona-Santiago.

Groupe Forrest International.desc: A family-owned group, legal entity Forrest Group International S.A. at Avenue Pasteur 9, Wavre, Belgium, which describes unique expertise in DR Congo and whose story begins with Malta Forrest at Kolwezi on 2 February 1922 and the public works and civil engineering business Entreprise Generale Malta Forrest. Its activities have included construction, cement (HeidelbergCement became majority shareholder of the Lukala cement works in 2010 and the group transferred its remaining shares in June 2015), Korongo Airlines (stopped in 2015), the Community Medical Centre hospital in Lubumbashi, Grelka's nearly 35,000 head of cattle on two ranches and off-grid solar power; since 2018 the group says it is no longer active in the mining sector. Malta David Forrest has been executive vice-president and chief executive since 2011.

Grupo Cobra (ACS).desc: The energy arm of the Spanish construction group ACS, doing engineering, procurement and construction work in the energy sector and holding greenfield concessions such as electricity transmission lines and power plants, with most of its ongoing projects in Latin America. The French construction and concessions group Vinci bought it for EUR 4.9 billion under a deal announced on 1 April 2021 and reported as completed by January 2022.

HKND Group (HK Nicaragua Canal Developme.desc: A privately held, newly formed Hong Kong-registered company, the Hong Kong Nicaragua Canal Development Investment Co. (HKND), chaired by Wang Jing, a private businessman who is also chairman and largest shareholder of Xinwei Telecom, a Chinese telecom company. Nicaraguan lawmakers granted it a 50-year canal concession in June 2013; CNN reported at the time that little is known about the company's structure or leadership team.

ExxonMobil affiliate (Area 4 operator).desc: ExxonMobil's own release states that the Area 4 exploration and production concession in Mozambique is held 70% by Mozambique Rovuma Venture S.p.A., an incorporated joint venture owned by ExxonMobil, Eni and CNPC, with ENH, Galp and Kogas each holding 10%, and that ExxonMobil will lead construction and operation of the liquefaction and related facilities while Eni leads the upstream facilities (December 2018). ExxonMobil Corporation itself is a United States oil, gas and chemicals company with principal executive offices in Spring, Texas and about 61,000 regular employees at the end of 2024.
